package_info.why_malicious: The Orion software update was compromised by attackers who inserted a sophisticated backdoor (Sunburst) into the build process. This supply chain attack distributed trojanized software to customers, enabling unauthorized remote access, data exfiltration, and espionage across affected environments.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (on service start or update install)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Implements a stealthy backdoor that, after a randomized delay, checks for network connectivity and beacons to a remote command-and-control (C2) server. Upon receiving an activation command, it downloads and executes additional attacker-supplied payloads, enabling further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code introduces a covert backdoor into a trusted software update, using delayed execution and process checks to evade detection. It establishes unauthorized outbound connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure and enables remote code execution, which is never expected in legitimate update logic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software updates should not contain logic for establishing C2 communications, delaying execution for days, or downloading and executing arbitrary code from the internet. Such behaviors are clear violations of software integrity and security best practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None. While legitimate update mechanisms may check for updates or send telemetry, they do not implement randomized long sleep intervals, beacon to unknown domains, or execute arbitrary remote code.
key_indicators: Randomized sleep interval (12-14 days) to evade sandbox and detection
Outbound network beaconing to attacker-controlled C2 domains
Conditional execution based on process name ('solarwinds.businesslayerhost')
Download and execution of remote payloads from within a signed, trusted DLL
Insertion of unauthorized logic into SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is covertly inserted into the Orion software build process, resulting in a trojanized SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll distributed via official updates.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of the backdoored DLL to customer environments through trusted update channels

attack_chain.action: Upon installation or service start, the malicious DLL executes, verifies it is running in the correct process context, and initiates a randomized sleep interval (12-14 days) to avoid detection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Stealthy persistence and evasion of automated analysis or sandboxing

attack_chain.action: After the delay, the backdoor checks for network connectivity and beacons to attacker-controlled C2 domains, awaiting further instructions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of covert communication channel with attacker infrastructure

attack_chain.action: If the C2 server responds with an activation command, the backdoor downloads and executes additional attacker-supplied payloads, enabling lateral movement, data exfiltration, or further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the victim environment, including potential data theft and further attacker actions

behavioral_signatures: Delayed execution (sleep for 12-14 days) after installation or service start
Network beaconing to previously unknown or attacker-controlled domains from Orion processes
Conditional execution based on process name ('solarwinds.businesslayerhost')
Download and execution of remote payloads from within a signed SolarWinds DLL
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with unexpected or unauthorized code sections
DLLs with cryptographic hashes differing from official SolarWinds releases
Presence of SolarWinds DLLs making unexpected outbound network connections
network_indicators: Connections to known Sunburst C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com)
Unusual DNS queries or HTTP(S) traffic from Orion servers to external IPs/domains not associated with SolarWinds
Beaconing patterns with long initial delays followed by periodic C2 communication
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor SolarWinds Orion DLLs, especially SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll, for unauthorized changes or unexpected code sections. Compare file hashes against known-good versions. Use EDR and network monitoring to detect delayed outbound connections or beaconing to suspicious domains (such as avsvmcloud.com) from Orion processes. Alert on any Orion process that downloads and executes code from the internet, or exhibits long sleep intervals prior to network activity. Investigate any unexpected outbound traffic from SolarWinds update processes.
